about: T16 evals (SPEC section 7). Each eval is a conversation: turns run in one Claude Code session (claude -p, then --resume). 'expect' is checked per turn: by script where the transcript or files can answer (commands, flags, PDF, numbers), by an LLM grader where meaning matters (must_say, questions, substitutes, edition vs country). 'reference' is the analyze call the turn should end with: its JSON is the truth for the baseline runs without the skill and warms the cache.

criteria.chain: script: the Wikipedia data came from the skill in the right order: a topic resolve before analyze (turn 'chain': resolve->analyze), analyze with no new topic resolve in follow-ups (analyze; resolve with --search-lang is a local search, not a new topic), resolve without analyze before an ambiguity question (resolve, no analyze), nothing analysed before a languages question (no analyze)
criteria.params: script: the last analyze call of the turn uses the expected QID (or, for learning English, not the namesake VOA programme Q2731224 that SPEC section 3 names as the wrong meaning), language editions, --rank-by and --report
criteria.answer_lang: script: every analyze call of the turn has the language of the user's messages (user_lang) in --answer-lang (default en) and, with --report, in --report-lang; turns without analyze are not applicable
criteria.must_say: grader: every must_say point of the turn's last analyze JSON (the reference JSON for baseline runs) reaches the answer with its meaning intact: editions, trend and confidence words, each number with its metric, negations
criteria.numbers: script evals/check_numbers.py: every number in the answer is in the JSON the skill printed in this conversation (result.json, resolve output), allowing for rounding; baseline runs are checked against the reference JSON; answers without numbers are not applicable
criteria.no_article_offer: grader, turns where an edition has no article: a substitute is offered for it (a broader concept or a closer local article) with how its meaning differs
criteria.questions: grader: exactly one clarifying question when the turn needs one (languages not named: with a proposed set; ambiguous name: listing the meanings), none otherwise; offers of next steps do not count
criteria.edition_not_country: grader: interest, audience or potential is attributed to language editions, not to countries ('Польща має потенціал' fails)
criteria.pdf: script: report.pdf was written during the turn when the user asked for a report
criteria.reply_lang: grader, extra: the reply is in the language of the user's messages (user_lang)

evals.name: ex1-fasting-pl-cs
evals.prompt: Порівняй зростання інтересу до інтервального голодування в польськомовній та чеськомовній Wikipedia за останні два роки.
evals.expected_output: resolve 'intermittent fasting' -> Q1666254; analyze pl,cs for 24 months with --answer-lang uk; cs falling with low confidence; pl no_article as a finding, with an offer: the broader 'fasting' (pl 'Post' is mostly religious fasting) and/or the pl-only 'Głodówka lecznicza' via --article; no question.

turns.prompt: Порівняй зростання інтересу до інтервального голодування в польськомовній та чеськомовній Wikipedia за останні два роки.

evals.name: ex2-astronomy-uk
evals.prompt: Ми думаємо додати курс з астрономії до освітнього застосунку. Чи зростає інтерес до цієї теми в україномовній Wikipedia, і наскільки цьому зростанню можна довіряти?
evals.expected_output: resolve 'astronomy' -> Q333 without a question (broad, not ambiguous); analyze uk with --answer-lang uk; interest is falling, with the confidence and its reason; one article stands for the whole topic.

evals.name: ex3-learning-english
evals.source: task example 3, verbatim; the languages are not named, so the first turn is one question with a proposed set; the answer is fixed so that runs compare
evals.prompt: Ми створюємо застосунок для вивчення мов. Порівняй інтерес до вивчення англійської у вибраних нами мовних розділах та підготуй короткий звіт: які аудиторії варто дослідити наступними й чому?
evals.expected_output: Turn 1: one question proposing a set of editions, nothing analysed. Turn 2: resolve the exact concept first, then a named proxy (no article on learning English as a foreign language in pl, cs, uk); analyze uk,pl,cs with --report and --answer-lang uk; PDF; the next audiences named as language editions, not countries or markets.

turns.prompt: Ми створюємо застосунок для вивчення мов. Порівняй інтерес до вивчення англійської у вибраних нами мовних розділах та підготуй короткий звіт: які аудиторії варто дослідити наступними й чому?

evals.name: ambiguous-java-en
evals.source: ambiguous name (SPEC section 3: Java = programming language or island), asked in English to check --answer-lang en
evals.prompt: Is interest in Java growing on Polish and Czech Wikipedia? Compare the last two years.
evals.expected_output: Turn 1: resolve says ambiguous: true -> one question listing the meanings, nothing analysed. Turn 2: analyze Q251 for pl,cs with --answer-lang en (or the default), answer in English.

turns.prompt: Is interest in Java growing on Polish and Czech Wikipedia? Compare the last two years.
